# `tcp`

`tcp` opens a TCP connection from the node to an address and port. The
check is healthy when the connection opens. When the `tcp` configuration is
written as a mapping, the check can also send a text and expect a reply.
The exchange is for a server that speaks a simple protocol of lines.

Choose `tcp` for a port that has to accept connections, such as the port of
a database server, and for a server of the team's own that answers a line of
text. A server that answers over UDP has [`udp`](udp.md). A program
that listens on a Unix socket, a file, has
[`unix_socket`](unix_socket.md). A service whose protocol MMWatchdog knows has
a module of its own, which checks more than the connection: such as
[`http`](http.md), [`tls`](tls.md), [`ssh`](ssh.md), and
[`smtp`](smtp.md).

## Inputs

A check writes the module's inputs as a mapping below the module's name. In place of the mapping, it can write one value after the name:

- the value of `tcp` (string): The address alone, as host:port, in place of the mapping of inputs.

The inputs of the mapping:

- `address` (string; required): The address to connect to, as host:port.
- `text_to_send` (string; optional): A text that the check sends once the connection is open. Without it the check sends nothing.
- `reply_contains` (string; optional): A text that the server's reply must contain. Without a rule for the reply, the check reads nothing.
- `reply_matches_regex` (string; optional): A regular expression that the server's reply must match.

## When the check fails, and when it cannot check

Without a rule for the reply, a run is healthy when the connection opens
and any configured `text_to_send` is sent,
with the message `TCP connection accepted`. The run fails when the
connection does not open. A connection can fail because no program listens
on the port or because a firewall refuses the connection. The run also
fails when the connection does not open within the check group's
`time_limit_per_run`. The message is the cause in the node's system's words,
such as `dial tcp 127.0.0.1:5432: connect: connection refused`, or, for a
connection that did not open in time, `the connection to 127.0.0.1:5432 did
not open within 5s (time_limit_per_run)`.

With `reply_contains`, `reply_matches_regex`, or both rules configured, a
run is healthy when the reply satisfies every configured rule.
The message is `the reply holds what the check expects`.
Besides a connection that does not open, the run fails when:

- **the reply fails at least one configured rule** when the server closes
  the connection or MMWatchdog has read 64 KiB. The message names the first
  unsatisfied rule: `the reply is not one that contains "READY"`, or
  `the reply is not one that matches the regular expression READY \d+ jobs`;
- **the reply still fails at least one configured rule when
  `time_limit_per_run` expires:** the message names the first unsatisfied
  rule, as in the preceding item, followed by
  `; MMWatchdog waited until the time limit of the run`;
- **the server sent nothing:** `the server sent no reply, and the check
  expects one that contains "READY"`;
- **the connection breaks in another way,** such as a reset by the server,
  with the cause in Go's words.

The failed run shows what the server sent, in its details and in the
[body of its alert](../alert-format.md), such
as `the server sent: myapp 1.0  READY 3 jobs`. In the displayed reply,
MMWatchdog replaces every control character and shortens the
reply to about 180 bytes.

A `tcp` check has no unknown result of its own: every answer of the server,
and every connection that does not open, is healthy or failed. Like every
check, a `tcp` check is unknown when the run does not end
([a run that does not end](../../how-it-works.md#a-run-that-does-not-end)). A
failed run starts or continues the check's
[failing time](../../how-to/decide-when-a-check-alerts.md). `tcp` reports no
measurement, so a `tcp` check takes no limit.

## Examples

### A port accepts a connection

```yaml
# /etc/mmwatchdog/check_groups/database_port.yml
check_groups:
  database_port:
    check_every: 30s
    time_limit_per_run: 5s
    alert_after_failing_for: 1m
    recovered_after_healthy_for: 30s
    tcp: 127.0.0.1:5432
    alert_severity: sos
```

The check is written directly on the check group, with the address alone as
the value of `tcp`, so status shows it as `database_port/tcp`. Every 30
seconds, MMWatchdog on the node connects to port 5432 of the node itself and closes
the connection again. MMWatchdog sends nothing and reads nothing. When no
connection has opened for 1 minute, MMWatchdog sends the `sos` alert.

### A server answers a text

```yaml
# /etc/mmwatchdog/check_groups/myapp_ports.yml
check_groups:
  myapp_ports:
    check_every: 30s
    time_limit_per_run: 5s
    alert_after_failing_for: 1m
    recovered_after_healthy_for: 30s
    checks:
      myapp_answers_ready_over_tcp:
        tcp:
          address: 127.0.0.1:7000
          text_to_send: "STATUS\r\n"
          reply_contains: READY
        alert_severity: sos
      myapp_greets_with_its_version:
        tcp:
          address: 127.0.0.1:7000
          reply_matches_regex: '^myapp 1\.'
        alert_severity: warn
```

In each run of the first check, MMWatchdog on the node connects to port 7000, sends
the line `STATUS`, and reads the reply until it contains `READY`. The run is
healthy as soon as the reply contains `READY`. MMWatchdog then closes the
connection. The second check sends nothing. MMWatchdog reads the server's
greeting for the second check. The second check is healthy when the
greeting starts with `myapp 1.`.

## How it works

- **The address is host:port,** with a port from 1 to 65535 and no default
  port. A host name with several addresses, such as `localhost` with one of
  each IP version, is tried at each address until a connection opens.
- **Written as a value,** `tcp: 127.0.0.1:5432`, the check only connects.
  Written as a mapping, the check takes `address` and the three inputs below.
- **`text_to_send` is sent once,** as soon as the connection is open. A text
  with a line break is written in double quotes, with `\r\n` or `\n` for the
  break, as the example shows: most line protocols expect one.
- **Without a rule, the check reads nothing,** also when it sends a text: it
  is healthy when the connection opens and any configured text is sent.
- **With a rule, the check reads until the rules hold,** and stops there, so
  a server that keeps the connection open does not hold the check up.
  MMWatchdog also stops reading when the server closes the connection,
  after reading 64 KiB, or at `time_limit_per_run`.
- **A check can state `reply_contains` and `reply_matches_regex`.** When a
  check states `reply_contains` and `reply_matches_regex`, the reply must
  satisfy each rule. `reply_contains` is a plain text.
  `reply_matches_regex` has the syntax of
  [RE2](https://github.com/google/re2/wiki/Syntax) and matches anywhere in
  the reply unless it is anchored, as `^myapp 1\.` is.
- **The check sends and matches text, not binary protocol messages.** A
  protocol that needs non-text bytes, such as DNS, needs a protocol-specific
  check ([`dns`](dns.md)) or a
  [module written by your team for your deployment project](../configuration-files.md#run-settings-of-a-shell-check-and-of-a-module-that-is-not-core).

## Errors and what they mean

`mmwatchdog validate` and `mmwatchdog reload` print each error after the file, the line, and
the column, which the table leaves out. The examples are for a check group `c` with a
direct `tcp` check.

| Message | What the message means, and what to do |
| --- | --- |
| `check_groups.c.tcp.address: address 127.0.0.1: missing port in address` | The address has no port. Write the address as host:port, such as `127.0.0.1:5432` |
| `check_groups.c.tcp.address: port must be a number from 1 to 65535` | The port is not a number from 1 to 65535 |
| `check_groups.c.tcp.address: missing port in address` | The mapping has no `address`, or it is empty |
| `check_groups.c.tcp.text_to_send: cannot be empty` | `text_to_send` is written with an empty text. Leave out `text_to_send` to send nothing |
| `check_groups.c.tcp.reply_contains: cannot be empty` | An empty `reply_contains` or `reply_matches_regex` is rejected |
| `check_groups.c.tcp.reply_matches_regex: is no valid regular expression: error parsing regexp: ...` | The regular expression is not valid RE2. The text after the colon says why |
| `check_groups.c.tcp.expect: unknown field "expect": the inputs of the module tcp are address, text_to_send, reply_contains, reply_matches_regex` | The mapping has an input that `tcp` does not have. Remove `expect`, or write an input that the message names |
| `check_groups.c.tcp: expected a mapping, or an address as host:port, found a list` | The check is written as a list. Write the address alone, such as `tcp: 127.0.0.1:5432`, or a mapping of the inputs |

## Tested on

- **Go tests** in `internal/checksandalerts`, each against a stand-in server
  on the test machine: `TestTCPCheckSendsATextAndExpectsAReply` (a reply in two parts,
  both rules, the greeting alone, a server that closes, one that says
  nothing until the time limit, a closed port, and validation),
  `TestChecksOfServersThatDoNotAnswerAsExpected` (a server that answers a
  part and waits, with what it sent in the details, and a port where
  nothing listens), and `TestTCPExchangePrimitive` in `internal/primitives`. They ran on macOS ARM64
  and, as the native suite, on the AMD64 guest of [every target distribution](../../changing-mmwatchdog/testing.md#every-target-distribution).
- **The acceptance suite** (`tests/integration/acceptance.py`), on [every target distribution](../../changing-mmwatchdog/testing.md#every-target-distribution): a `tcp` check with the address alone,
  healthy against a test service, also with MMX absent at runtime.
- **The services suite** (`tests/integration/service_scenarios.py`), on [every target distribution](../../changing-mmwatchdog/testing.md#every-target-distribution): a small TCP server of the test, with a
  check that sends a text and keeps both rules, one that reads the
  greeting, one that expects a text that never comes, with what the server
  sent in its details, and a refused connection once the server is stopped.
- **Not verified on a real node:** a server that answers a part and then
  waits. Go tests cover a server that answers a part and then waits ([validation record](../../changing-mmwatchdog/validation.md#not-verified-for-this-build)).

## Why it works this way

- **A reply rule needs at least one received byte.** A regular expression
  that matches empty text cannot make a silent server healthy.

- **No default port.** A reader sees on each check where it connects
  ([protocols and common server software](../../changing-mmwatchdog/design/checks.md#protocols-and-common-server-software)).
- **The check reads until the rules hold, not until the server closes.** A
  server of a line protocol often keeps the connection open, and the check
  must not wait for it until the time limit.
- **Without a reply rule, MMWatchdog reads nothing.** A port that accepts
  connections is all that such a check asks, and a server that sends
  nothing first is still healthy.
- **What the server sent is in the alert.** A reader sees at once whether
  the server said something else or nothing.
- **MMWatchdog reads at most 64 KiB of a reply,** whatever the server sends.
